main_text.p: īnnumera & maxima punitur, & quæ instantium pœnarum adhuc minima sit, objicit, sic ut omnibus illis ferendis par non possit esse. Hinc cruciatus & morsus conscientiæ quidem innumeri in tali animo furgunt, at non est tristitia secundum Deum, quem (juxta th. 5. hujus) nunquam agnovit, sed ejus loco Principem summé iratum, & implacabilem; ignem & flammam consumentem & simile quid imaginans, præ anxietate quò se vertat non habet, ubique quasi spectris illi occurrentibus, quæ interius imaginationi ejus Diabolus obtrudit. Inter tot mala & spectra ergo quasi versans, quorum quodlibet morte multò horribiliorem judicat, facilè suam sententiam mutat, & quia mortuos judicat nullos dolores ampliùs sentire, & quæ de vita alia post mortem sæpius audivit, esse nugas, nec futuram talem unquam resurrectionem &c: inter omnia mala hoc minimum esse concludit mori & finire morte dolores, & quidem subito, ut quasi mortem, seu terriculum illud crudele præveniat, ne ab illo diutius totqueatur. Et sic Diabolus tragœdiam suam finit.

page.notes: The right edge is cut away; the partly visible column of the next page at the right is not transcribed. Some letters in the first lines are faint, notably "īnnumera" (possibly "innumera" with a macron) and "quò" (read as "quò"). Words such as "sed", "non" and "Principem" are read as printed; the printed "summe" is rendered "summé". Marginal notes at the right edge are cut off and only fragments are visible (e.g. "8.", "me", "fpi", "tri"); they are not transcribed. The first word of the first line is partly cut off at the top. The line "medum" is as printed and may be a misprint for "modum"; uncertain.
